item.title: TIMES SHOPPER | Clothes clean and smelling good
item.description: For generations, Fijian households have relied on trusted, no-nonsense products to keep families looking their best – from crisp school uniforms in Suva to work attires and everyday wear across our maritime communities. OMO 800g laundry detergent powder has steadily earned its place in this everyday routine, and it’s worth understanding why this particular detergent along with its formula resonate
item.content:encoded:
For generations, Fijian households have relied on trusted, no-nonsense products to keep families looking their best – from crisp school uniforms in Suva to work attires and everyday wear across our maritime communities.

OMO 800g laundry detergent powder has steadily earned its place in this everyday routine, and it’s worth understanding why this particular detergent along with its formula resonates so strongly with local consumers.

Fiji’s tropical climate is tough on fabric. Perspiration, outdoor activity, and the ever-present challenge of mildew in tropical conditions mean detergents need to work extra harder than they might in temperate markets.

OMO’s powder formulation is designed to tackle deep-set stains — grass, mud, food, and sweat — which makes it a practical fit for households with active children, market vendors, farmers, and tradespeople whose clothing takes a real beating during the day.

Because a large share of Fijian households, particularly in peri-urban and rural areas, still hand-wash a significant portion of their laundry, a powder detergent that dissolves effectively and rinses clean, even in cooler water, offers genuine everyday value.

This is a meaningful point of difference from liquid detergents, which can be less economical for hand-washing large loads.

Our OMO 800g Pack: A smart middle ground

Pack size matters enormously in the Fiji market, where household budgets are managed carefully and weekly or fortnightly shopping trips are the norm.

The 800g pack sits in a practical middle ground: substantial enough to serve a family for multiple wash cycles, yet accessible in price compared to bulk 2kg or 5kg formats that require a larger upfront outlay.

For extended families, a common household structure across Fiji, this size supports frequent top-up purchases without straining the budget, while still offering better value per wash than smaller sachets.

OMO, under the Unilever stable, is distributed by Motibhai Group of Companies- Sharing Quality, Sharing Happiness. It benefits from decades of brand recognition throughout the Pacific.

In a market where trust is often built through word-of-mouth and generational habit – “what mum used, I use” – this legacy matters.

What ultimately sets OMO apart in Fiji is not a single standout feature, but how well the format and performance align with the realities of Fijian household life — the climate, the washing habits, and the budgeting patterns that define daily routines.

For brands and retailers looking to communicate value in this market, that alignment is the real story worth telling.

item.title: TIMES SHOPPER | Healthy foods on a budget
item.description: EATING for better heart health does not have to mean spending more at the grocery store. For many families, the weekly grocery bill is a major household expense, and with the rising cost of everyday essentials, finding the right balance between nutritious food and affordability can be challenging.
item.content:encoded:
EATING for better heart health does not have to mean spending more at the grocery store.

For many families, the weekly grocery bill is a major household expense, and with the rising cost of everyday essentials, finding the right balance between nutritious food and affordability can be challenging.

A heart-healthy diet generally focuses on foods such as fruits and vegetables, whole grains, beans, lentils, nuts, fish and other lean sources of protein, while limiting excessive amounts of saturated fat, added sugar and salt.

The good news is that many of these foods are also among the most affordable options available.

The secret is not necessarily buying expensive “health foods” or searching for a particular superfood. Instead, it is about making thoughtful decisions before and during your grocery trip.

One of the simplest ways to save money while eating healthier is to plan meals before going shopping.

Rather than walking through the supermarket and deciding what to buy as you go, take a few minutes each week to plan breakfasts, lunches and dinners. Begin by checking what you already have in your pantry, refrigerator and freezer.

You may discover that you already have rice, pasta, canned beans, frozen vegetables, oats or other ingredients that can form the basis of several meals.

Once you know what is available, build your meal plan around those ingredients and look for items that are on special.

For example, if chicken, vegetables or certain fruits are discounted that week, consider building several meals around them. Planning according to what is already in your kitchen and what is available at a good price can help reduce unnecessary spending.

Meal planning can also prevent the temptation to order takeaway food when you are tired or short on time.

A grocery list may seem simple, but it can make a significant difference to both your health and your wallet.

Once your meals are planned, write down exactly what you need. Organising your list according to supermarket sections, such as produce, meat, dairy and pantry items, can make shopping faster and easier.

Most importantly, try to stick to the list.

Supermarkets are designed to encourage additional purchases. Special displays, snacks near the checkout and products placed at eye level can make it easy to add items that were never part of your original plan.

A shopping list helps keep your attention on the foods your household actually needs.

If you use your phone while shopping, consider creating a digital grocery list. Checking items off as you go can help you stay organised and reduce impulse purchases.

Fresh produce is an important part of a healthy diet, but it is not the only option.

Frozen fruits and vegetables can be affordable, convenient and nutritious choices. Many frozen fruits and vegetables are processed and frozen soon after harvesting, helping preserve much of their nutritional value.

Frozen vegetables such as peas, spinach, mixed vegetables and broccoli can be kept for much longer than fresh produce. This can be particularly useful for families who struggle with food waste.

Frozen foods can also save preparation time. Having chopped vegetables or frozen fruit available means you can quickly prepare a stir-fry, soup, smoothie or side dish without having to wash and cut everything from scratch.

Choose plain frozen fruits and vegetables where possible. Some frozen products contain added sauces, sugar or significant amounts of salt, which can make them less suitable for a heart-conscious eating pattern.

Canned foods can also be valuable additions to a budget-friendly kitchen.

Canned beans, lentils, chickpeas, tomatoes and fish can provide affordable ingredients for a wide range of meals.

Beans and lentils are particularly useful because they provide protein and fibre while generally costing less than many meat products.

Canned tuna and salmon can also provide protein and beneficial omega-3 fats. They can be added to salads, sandwiches, rice dishes or pasta for a quick and inexpensive meal.

When purchasing canned foods, look for options with little or no added salt where possible. If regular canned beans are the only option available, rinsing them before eating can help reduce some of the sodium.

Protein is an important part of a balanced diet, but meat and seafood can sometimes take up a significant portion of the grocery budget.

Instead of relying on one protein source, try diversifying your choices throughout the week.

Eggs are a versatile and relatively affordable source of high-quality protein. They can be used for breakfast, added to salads or vegetables, or turned into a quick dinner when combined with other ingredients.

item.title: TIMES SHOPPER | Knowing the good fats from the bad
item.description: Low-fat diets, high-fat diets, seed oils, anti-inflammatory fats, essential fats… while doing your own research about nutrition, I’m sure you must have heard a lot about fats. The information out there might be a bit confusing though, with so much conflicting advice and people swearing by the miracle approach they found.
item.content:encoded:
Low-fat diets, high-fat diets, seed oils, anti-inflammatory fats, essential fats… while doing your own research about nutrition, I’m sure you must have heard a lot about fats.

The information out there might be a bit confusing though, with so much conflicting advice and people swearing by the miracle approach they found.

So, today we’ll be talking about fat, starting from the basics.

What are fats and why do they have such a bad reputation?

Fats are a type of macronutrient, which means a nutrient we eat in large quantities daily, together with carbohydrates and protein.

In terms of weight gain, eating a large quantity of fat is often one of the main causes why we tend to put on weight.

And this is not surprising, as eating 1 g of fat provides 9 kcal, more than double the amount produced by 1 g of protein or carbohydrates.

And because we put on weight when we eat more calories than we burn in our daily activities, eating a large quantity of high-calorie foods like fried or fatty foods is often one of the main causes of weight gain.

Does it make a difference which type of fat you eat?

However, even though we speak about fats as a single group, it contains different types of fat, some of which are more beneficial than others.

The types of fat that are generally considered more harmful are, in descending order, trans fats, saturated fats, and cholesterol.

In fact, their excessive consumption can raise your level of blood cholesterol, increase the risk of NCDs such as heart disease, type 2 diabetes, or certain types of cancer, and create inflammation.

On the other hand, monounsaturated fats from avocados and olive oil for example, are considered beneficial in moderate quantities, in particular for the health of your heart and to prevent and manage type 2 diabetes. Polyunsaturated fats, found in particular in nuts and seeds, are also considered protective since they are anti-inflammatory and their regular consumption helps prevent heart disease and cognitive decline.

Notably, including good sources of Omega-3 and Omega-6 fatty acids in your daily diet is highly recommended because these are the only two types of fat that are essential.

This means that your body cannot produce them on its own, and you therefore have to get them through your food.

In particular, you should check your consumption of Omega-3s as a group to ensure you intentionally include reliable sources in your routine, as the number of sources is limited. These include: walnuts, flax or chia seeds, seaweed, fish products, and soy.

Omega-6s, on the other hand, are more common, as they are found in nuts, seeds, and many types of oils.

Should you reduce the amount of fat you eat? If you tend to eat large quantities of high-fat foods, like fried foods, cakes, industrially baked goods, ready meals, or store-bought sauces, then the answer is yes—reducing the total amount of fat is definitely necessary in this case.

However, eliminating or restricting fat too much from your diet is not necessary and not suitable. You should try and focus on the more beneficial types of fats (Omega-3s, Omega-6s, polyunsaturated and monounsaturated fats) and reduce the other types like saturated fats and dietary cholesterol.

However, here again, saturated fats and cholesterol play key roles in our body, so the aim is not necessarily to eliminate them, but to reduce their consumption mainly by eating less fried and processed foods.

Trans fats, on the other hand, are a different story. They provide no health benefits and should be avoided as much as possible.

Choosing sources such as olive oil can be part of a balanced approach to dietary fats. Picture: www.brownhealth.org

item.title: TIMES SHOPPER | Create a home you enjoy
item.description: CREATING a comfortable and welcoming home begins with choosing furniture that combines style, practicality and durability. The lounge and dining areas are among the most important spaces in any home, providing places where families relax, entertain guests, enjoy meals and spend quality time together.
item.content:encoded:
CREATING a comfortable and welcoming home begins with choosing furniture that combines style, practicality and durability.

The lounge and dining areas are among the most important spaces in any home, providing places where families relax, entertain guests, enjoy meals and spend quality time together.

For households looking to refresh their interiors, Overseas Lounge & Dining offers a variety of furniture options designed to complement modern lifestyles while providing everyday comfort and value.

From spacious lounge suites to stylish dining sets, the right furniture can transform an ordinary room into a warm and inviting space.

The lounge is often the heart of the home. It is where families gather after a busy day, watch television, welcome visitors or simply sit back and relax.

Overseas Lounge furniture combines modern designs with comfortable seating, making it suitable for everyday family use.

Whether you are furnishing a new home, upgrading an existing living room or creating a comfortable entertainment area, there are designs to suit different needs and preferences.

A major consideration when choosing a lounge suite is comfort.

Seating should provide enough space for family members and guests while offering the support needed for everyday use.

Spacious designs are particularly useful for larger households or families who regularly entertain.

At the same time, more compact options can be suitable for apartments and smaller living areas where making the most of available space is important.

Quality finishes for different interiors

Furniture is not only about functionality; its appearance can have a major influence on the overall look and feel of a room.

Overseas Lounge offers a range of upholstery finishes, including fabric, air leather and semi-leather-look options.

These choices allow homeowners to select a finish that matches their lifestyle, existing furniture and preferred interior style.

Colours and designs can also be selected to complement different décor themes. Whether your home features a contemporary, classic or minimalist interior, choosing furniture that coordinates with existing pieces can help create a more unified appearance.

For homeowners who like to change their décor over time, neutral colours can provide flexibility, while bolder shades can become a statement feature within the room.

A beautiful lounge suite needs to be more than attractive. It also needs to withstand everyday use.

Strong frame construction is an important consideration when purchasing lounge furniture, particularly for families where sofas are used regularly. Durable construction can help furniture maintain its comfort and appearance over time.

A lounge suite should fit naturally into the space without making the room feel overcrowded. Before purchasing, homeowners should consider the size of the room, the number of people who will regularly use the furniture and how much space is needed to move comfortably around it.

For apartments, smaller homes and offices, appropriately sized furniture can provide comfort without taking up unnecessary floor space. Larger homes and entertainment areas may benefit from spacious lounge arrangements that provide plenty of seating for family and visitors.

While the lounge provides a place to relax, the dining area brings people together around the table.

Whether it is the family’s everyday breakfast, a quick weekday dinner or a special meal with friends, a dining table is often at the centre of shared moments.

Overseas Dining offers stylish dining sets designed to suit modern homes, with different table sizes available to accommodate different household requirements.

For smaller families or compact dining areas, a smaller table can provide sufficient seating while helping maximise available space. Larger households may prefer more spacious dining sets that provide room for everyone to sit comfortably.

The design of the table can also contribute to the overall character of the dining area.

Dining furniture is exposed to everyday wear and tear, from regular meals and family gatherings to accidental spills and frequent cleaning.

For this reason, durability and easy maintenance are important factors when choosing a dining set.

Overseas Dining features table designs incorporating materials such as wood, metal and mixed-material finishes.

These options provide homeowners with flexibility when matching their dining furniture with the rest of their interior.

From messy feeding times to routine diaper changes, keeping a baby clean and comfortable is a daily priority for families.

Parents are constantly on the lookout for reliable, skin-friendly baby care products that stand up to dry, humid, tropical climates while remaining gentle on delicate infant skin.

This is where Huggies Clean Care Wipes (80s) come in, a trusted solution now making waves across local households.

Fiji’s climate means that babies are often prone to sweat, heat rashes, and skin irritation.

Choosing the right wipes is critical to maintaining a healthy skin barrier.

Huggies Clean Care Wipes are crafted with skin-loving natural fibers that efficiently trap mess while remaining extraordinarily soft.

Unlike rough alternatives that can aggravate reactive skin, these wipes provide a thick, cushiony texture that cleans effectively with fewer passes.

Formulated to handle everyday chaos, they offer a 4X cleaner feel, making quick work of everything from sticky fruit juices after a day at daycare to unexpected diaper blowouts at home.

In today’s economic climate, families appreciate brands that deliver premium performance without stretching household budgets.

The Huggies Clean Care Wipes 80-pack strikes the ideal balance between high-end quality and everyday affordability.

Generous Pack Size, each pack contains 80 moist, durable sheets, making it ideal to keep stationed at home on the changing table or tossed into a diaper bag for outings around town.

Convenient Dispensing, the resealable moisture lock lid ensures that every single wipe stays fresh, wet, and ready to use from the first sheet to the very last.

While designed with diaper changes in mind, the versatility of Huggies Clean Care Wipes makes them an essential multi-purpose tool for Fijian parents on the go. Busy mothers and fathers utilise them for:

Quick Hand and Face Cleanups: Perfect for wiping away sticky fingers after snacks or outdoor play.

Surface Wipe-Downs: Handy for a quick cleanup of highchairs, toys, or stroller handles when travelling.

Travel Companion: Lightweight and compact enough to fit effortlessly into backpacks, handbags, and travel kits for weekend trips across the islands.

When it comes to your baby’s comfort, settling for second best is never an option. Huggies combines decades of global expertise with ingredients designed to protect and nurture your little one’s skin.

Huggies is a product of Kimberly-Clark and is distributed by the Motibhai Group- sharing quality, sharing Happiness.

Give your baby the gentle, skin-loving care they deserve because when it comes to your little one, “We got you, baby”.
